### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6de301737e7505c06e3653fb21ff6427a81122f2` — the merge of head `f4edf7037bbbd16e75ca46e20f4cb49b67b0f764` into base `2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6de301737e7505c06e3653fb21ff6427a81122f2 && git checkout 6de301737e7505c06e3653fb21ff6427a81122f2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9 f4edf7037bbbd16e75ca46e20f4cb49b67b0f764 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9 && git merge --no-ff f4edf7037bbbd16e75ca46e20f4cb49b67b0f764

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2c5b90db052ee980fb6cf8e1d7dabbd87b99c1d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f4edf7037bbbd16e75ca46e20f4cb49b67b0f764`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/record-page-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-removal-routes.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-removal-route-ledger.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/affordanceGrants.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx, content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx

Inputs read: card #35724 body and all five comments (triage 7029758904, claim 7077769852, dev reports 7079248362, 7079463814, 7079944559), PR #36458 body, file list and net diff at the head, the check-runs on the head (62 success, 11 skipped, one cancelled PR-body guards run whose rerun on this head is success; nothing failing or pending). Code outside the diff was read on the main checkout only: `packages/core/src/security/own-row-delete-routes.ts`, `packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts`, `attachment-files-opt-in.ts`, `attachment-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-attachment.object.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, the plugin-security middleware registration, and the HTTP server contract.

### ① Derived judgments

- New route `PATCH /api/v1/attachments/:id`, body exactly `file_name`. Right: a new door, ledgered as a `gap` row beside the removal door, and the conformance test enumerates both.
- New capability: the uploader renames their own attachment with no edit grant on `sys_attachment`. Right, and it is the widening the card asks for ("same permission as Delete: uploader or parent editor"); it mirrors the removal door's elevation line for line.
- A rename by anyone else adds no capability: it is the update the data door already admits (edit grant, then the update gate's uploader-or-parent-editor row rule), reached through a second route. Right.
- The record page payload's `attachments` rows now carry `uploaded_by` expanded where the reader may read the user, and the stored id otherwise. Right as a change the response schema admits (`RecordPageStreamRowsSchema` rows are open records), and it is the same expansion the `activity` part already makes of `actor_id`. A consumer that compared the field with an id must read `.id`; the changeset says so.
- `@object-ui/core` `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS` gains `attachmentRename` (`crud: null`, grant `update`). Right: an added row, with its census expectation.
- `mountAttachmentRemovalDoor` now mounts neither door on a server lacking DELETE or PATCH. Right: the `IHttpServer` contract declares both verbs, so no conforming server loses the removal door.
- No Zod shape changes in `record-page.zod.ts`: prose only. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) is correct on the PR body and the changeset, and Metadata-protocol: none is correct (nothing an author can write changes). Patch on `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/core` follows the rule that a non-protocol change ships patch. Check Changeset is success on the head.

N1 (nit): `@objectstack/spec` is not in the changeset although its JSDoc (which ships in the declarations) and its generated reference page changed. Prose only, the gate accepted it; left as an accepted deviation.
N2 (nit): the changeset says "no answer narrowed" while its own second bullet tells a consumer of `uploaded_by` to read `.id`. The note is there, so the reader is served; the opening sentence is slightly generous.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (delete grant without edit grant): answered by the seat as B, then B again on the uploader row. Implemented in the panel as `canDelete` and (edit grant or the row's uploader is the caller). The server is unchanged by both rulings, which is correct: see section ④.
- Open question 2 (bare id reaching a reader refused `sys_user`): answered A. The engine's stored form stays, and the panel renders no id, no name and no title; pinned.
- Rework 1 question (uploader row exemption): answered B, implemented, pinned for a bare id and an expanded value.
- Docs follow-up from the first report: done in this PR (`attachments-access.mdx`).
- Download keeps the original `sys_file` name after a rename: declared in the PR and in the docs, not filed. Accepted.
- Deviations (files outside the claim, refusal code `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for the new verb, the two census files): each explained and each follows from where the producer or the census lives. Accepted.
- Process note for the seat: the two rulings are not comments on the card thread; this record takes them from the dev reports that quote them (7079463814, 7079944559).
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The door is one by-id read and one by-id write; the uploader name comes from the engine's own expand, the mechanism the activity part already uses.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/record-page.zod.ts`: the two edited sentences say the `attachments` part is the `sys_attachment` read "with `$count` and its uploader expanded" and, in the table, "`uploaded_by` expanded". The route does exactly that: `answerAttachments` passes `expand: relationMap(['uploaded_by'])` through the same `readStream` the activity part uses, so the surrounding sentence ("asked of the data door as the caller") still holds for the expansion. The first consumer (the panel) reads both the expanded and the bare form, and its own fallback list read asks the same `$expand`, so the part stays "the read it replaces". The JSDoc matches what the server serves. The JSDoc makes no statement about rename, so there is nothing in it to hold against the rename door.

Server-side authorization of the rename, judged on `renameAttachment` against the update gate on main:

- The rule is enforced on the server, not only in the panel. The row is read as the caller first (grant, organization wall, parent-derived read visibility), and an unreadable row answers the unknown id's 404.
- Uploader limb: the only thing that admits the elevated write is `row.uploaded_by === callerId` on the row just read as the caller. `uploaded_by` is server-stamped on create and `readonly` on update, so a caller cannot make themselves the uploader. A hidden, null or expanded value fails the comparison and falls to the caller limb, so it fails closed. The elevated write carries only `file_name`, so the gates it skips (re-point, file reference, files opt-in) have nothing to judge, and the row rule it skips would have passed the uploader anyway. The column's length rule is the record validator's and is not skipped.
- Caller limb: `engine.update` as the caller. plugin-security's check is an engine middleware every operation passes, and the attachment `beforeUpdate` gate runs `authorizeRows`, the same function the delete gate runs. So the edit grant and uploader-or-parent-editor decide, as the door's JSDoc says.
- The handler is the removal door's handler step for step (caller resolution, anonymous refusal, held sign-in, no query, id, then the body), and the body admits one key with a non-blank string.
- API-key scopes on this platform add permissions and never narrow, and the door accepts no OAuth token, so the elevation opens nothing through a narrower credential.

The UI gate is narrower than the server in two places, both correct and both stated in the docs page: the server asks no delete grant on either limb (the uploader limb needs no grant at all, and an edit-grant parent editor without the delete grant can already rename through the data door), while the panel asks the delete grant first. The panel offers one case the server refuses (delete and edit grants, not the uploader, not a parent editor), which the panel cannot see and answers in words.

`content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`, the door's JSDoc, the ledger note and the changeset all describe the same rule as the code, sentence by sentence, including the five refusal codes.

N3 (nit): `affordanceGrants.ts` says the panel asks the `attachmentRename` row "only for rows the caller did not upload". The panel resolves it once per render and tests it before the uploader comparison. The verdict is identical for every row; only the sentence is looser than the code.
N4 (nit): `sys_attachment.file_name` is still described on main as a "Denormalised copy of sys_file.name"; after this door it can differ. A follow-up wording fix, outside this diff.
N5 (nit): the grant-dependent answers of the door (uploader with no edit grant 200, non-uploader without the grant 403) are pinned against a fixture middleware standing in for plugin-security, and no pin exercises a name over 255 characters. The lane seat's remainder; a dogfood pin on the real stack would be the stronger form.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 席位核对

L1 (L1-e) on head `f4edf7037b`, card #35724: **ACCEPT**, with one landing condition (body only). The contract-tier L2 owns the depth reading of the door's elevation.

**Landing condition.** The panel still offers Delete only to a holder of the `sys_attachment` delete grant (`attachmentDelete`, through `dataSource.delete`). The member grant is `{ allowRead, allowCreate }` (`attachment-member-grant.ts:66`). So a member who uploaded a file is offered neither Delete nor Rename on it, although both doors admit them: the removal door since #33010, and this PR's rename door. As a result, `canRename`'s uploader limb never reaches a member.
- This is the "console half" the ledger names ("it moves to this route in the console half of the same ruling"). I found no open card for it.
- This PR makes the gap wider by one verb. It does not cause it. Rename follows the panel's existing `canDelete`, as the card's "a reader who may delete" reads, and the docs say so plainly ("offers Rename to a reader who holds the delete grant").
- Before landing, file a card, or name an existing one, for "the Attachments tab offers a member neither Delete nor Rename on their own upload". Add "carried by #N" to the Acceptance notes.

**Read**
- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36458`): open, draft, base `main`, `Fixes #35724`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
  - The face flags `changeset` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@object-ui/plugin-form`. The spec touch is JSDoc prose in `record-page.zod.ts` with no Zod shape change. The plugin-form touch is one test expectation. Neither owes an entry.
  - Gates: 62 success, 11 expected skip. The one `cancelled` PR-body guards row superseded at this head is not a red.
- **`Fixes` is right.**
  - Done-when 1: the record page payload's `attachments` part and the panel's own list read both expand `uploaded_by`, as the caller. A reader who may read the user gets the row. One who may not keeps the stored id, which the panel never renders (`uploaderOf`: an object's `name`, the viewer's own name, else `''`). Both sides are pinned.
  - Done-when 2: Rename persists, pinned end to end on both halves. The panel sends `PATCH /api/v1/attachments/:id` with exactly `{ file_name }` (trimmed), and the door stores it and answers `{ id, file_name }`. A reader who may not delete sees no Rename, pinned and ablated.
- **The door.** It reads as the caller first (`findOne` with `context`), so a row out of sight is `404` alike with an unknown id. Then it uses one of two limbs:
  - The uploader (`uploaded_by === callerId`, the only test that admits elevation) writes under `isSystem` with `attributedUserId` and the caller's `tenantId`. That is the removal door's elevation for the same ruling (6879388034).
  - Anyone else updates as the caller, so the edit grant and the update gate (whose row rule is the delete rule) judge it.
  - The body takes exactly `file_name` (non-blank, trimmed). Query parameters are refused, and unknown keys are refused, not ignored. An update that matches nothing answers `404`, not `200`.
  - Refusals carry `code` and `status` (the ADR-0112 envelope), asserted in the integration test, for example `[403, 'RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE']`.
- **Ruling B** (`canRename = canDelete && (edit grant || uploader)`) matches the door exactly: anyone else's rename needs the edit grant. It goes through the new `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS.attachmentRename` row, so the census holds without an OUT_OF_FAMILY entry. Both limbs are ablated red.
- **Scope.** The surface reached outside the claim (the record-page producer, the spec prose and its generated page, the tenant-audit census, the dogfood stream test, the grants row) is each named in the body with its reason, and each follows from the expand or the census.
- **Sentences, checked one by one.** The changeset, `attachments-access.mdx` (the code table, the limbs, "only the name the attachment is listed under changes") and `record-page.mdx` are true of the diff. The consumer note in the changeset (`uploaded_by.id` where the reader may read the user) is the one shape change, and the panel's own comparisons read both forms.
